title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། བེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 184)
shelf_note: A Pramāṇa commentary (discussion of time, direct perception and inference, with lemmata cited by ཞེས་བྱ་བ / ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ) in the Derge Tengyur Tshad ma section; belongs on the shelf.

ocr_errors.image: line 7 is visibly longer between འཛིན་པ་ and ཁྱད་པར; it appears to read approx. འཛིན་པ་ནི་འཁྲུལ་པ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ ('no different from error')
ocr_errors.problem: a word (apparently 'error', འཁྲུལ་པ) dropped, leaving 'no distinction' with no term of comparison

ocr_errors.image: the cluster after ལས is hard to resolve at this resolution; the reading is plausible but uncertain

tr_errors_A.problem: the page-initial fragment (end of a word from the previous page) is filled out with a guessed verb

tr_errors_A.english: This is explained in the commentary beginning with the words "Time is valid cognition."
tr_errors_A.problem: 'commentary' for what is a lemma from the root text; 'independent time' also added to དུས

tr_errors_B.english: That which is free from <note>the object</note> does not exist.
tr_errors_B.problem: the note supplies 'the object' as referent of དེ, an interpretation not on the page

tr_errors_B.english: there would be no distinction <note>between presence and absence</note>
tr_errors_B.problem: invented note fills the missing term of comparison with a wrong guess (the image appears to say 'no different from error')

tr_errors_B.english: the aspect of staying in front
tr_errors_B.problem: awkward literalism for 'the aspect present before one'

pages.prefer_reason: Both are faithful in argument with no serious errors, but B adds two interpretive notes not on the page (one a wrong guess at the comparison term), while A's 'no distinction from error' matches what the image appears to say.

book_verdict: Right leaf with a good transcription (one probable dropped word); both English versions follow the argument on time and perception faithfully, A slightly cleaner than B, which adds speculative notes.
